entradas.text: It was a dark, chilly evening when Petr called and asked if we could meet. He gave no details -- all he said was that it was important.

I drove alone through Holsord's suburbs until I reached the meeting point he named: 147 Wruhec Avenue, number 26. Our old campaign headquarters, untouched since the night of the election. This was where everything began.

I made my way up the dusty staircase of the office building. The light in the second-floor hallway was out, so I used a cigarette lighter to find my way to the wooden door marked 26. I pulled on the handle, but it wouldn't budge. The heavy door had always been a pain to open.
“Coming.”
Petr pushed on the door with all his weight. It made a screeching sound as it opened.
“Without further ado, I bid you welcome to this grand nostalgia trip, hosted by yours truly, Petr Vectern!"
“Feeling sentimental yet?”
“Not really. It's just an office.”
entradas.menu: “Not really. It's just an office.”

entradas.text: “Indeed. I haven't been to this place in ages!”
entradas.menu: “Indeed. I haven't been to this place in ages!”

entradas.text: He made an exaggerated bow. The dust from the opened door was still settling down.
“I remember it as being much cleaner.”
entradas.menu: “I remember it as being much cleaner.”

entradas.text: “That's what time does to things, my friend. You're looking a little shabbier yourself than you did back then."
“Well, I for one am overflowing with nostalgia.”
“I miss it sometimes. Even that damn door.”
“Come over here. Remember this?”

He walked over to his old desk and pointed to the gramophone that had annoyed our neighbors and kept us company for so many late nights. Petr filpped the switch, and it filled the room with swing music from the '20s.
“I'll be damned. It still works.”
“So, what are we celebrating?”
entradas.menu: “So, what are we celebrating?”

entradas.text: “Are you going to tell me why we are here?”
entradas.menu: “Are you going to tell me why we are here?”

entradas.text: “I thought this office was sold off.”
entradas.menu: “I thought this office was sold off.”

entradas.text: “Life, my friend. Life.”
“No, I've been paying the rent. Too many memories attached to this place just to sell it. And you know, we might use it again soon..."
“In a bit.”
He put his hand under the desk and brought a bottle out. He took a swig out of it and passed the bottle to me.
I took a swig as well before passing the bottle back to Petr.
entradas.menu: Drink.

entradas.text: “Aren't there any glasses?”
entradas.menu: “Aren't there any glasses?”

entradas.text: “Palace life is pampering you too much. Just drink from the bottle like the old days. Remember where we come from.”
“That's my boy.”
Petr snapped his fingers to the music while going through the items in the room. It looked virtually unchanged since election night.
“Come on, have a look around. See if it doesn't bring back memories."
I made my way to the gramophone and started flipping through the records next to it.
entradas.menu: Go through the records next to the gramophone.

entradas.text: I walked over to the tower of storage boxes and opened one of them.
entradas.menu: Look through the storage boxes.

entradas.text: I walked over to my old desk, sat down on the squeaky chair and opened the top drawer.
entradas.menu: Check your old desk drawers.

entradas.text: Inside, there were a few old coins, pencils and sheets of paper. Underneath them, something caught my eye.
It was a photograph of me and Monica, sitting under a tree. This must've been 10, maybe 15 years ago. We looked so young and so happy. Monica would love to see this.
“Nice find. Look at baby Anton! You didn't even have your iconic look.”
I took the photograph and slid it into my jacket pocket.
entradas.menu: Take the photograph.

entradas.text: I put the photograph back into the desk drawer.
entradas.menu: Put the photograph back.

entradas.text: In one of the storage boxes, I found a heavy object, wrapped safely. I unwrapped it.

It was an emerald-colored statue of a goat, the symbol of Sordland. I remembered that this was a gift from Brenda: one of the '53 election campaign assistants. It would look good on my desk in the palace.
“Brenda, Brenda, Brenda. Always sucking up to you, and where did it get her? Seriously, where? I have no idea where she ended up."
I left the statue where it was.
entradas.menu: Leave the statue.

entradas.text: I lifted the storage box with the statue in it and put it near the door so I could take it on the way out.
entradas.menu: Take the statue.

entradas.text: I found one of my favourite albums ever: Mountains by Janit Gurz. A set of plaintive folk songs that made me yearn for the countryside whenever I heard it.
“What a classic! You should mail that to Franc so he can learn what real music is.”
I left the record where it was.
entradas.menu: Leave the record.

entradas.text: I pulled the record out, put it under my arm and placed it next to the door.
entradas.menu: Take the record.

entradas.text: “You said you wanted to talk about something on the phone.”
entradas.menu: “You said you wanted to talk about something on the phone.”

entradas.text: “You called me here just for nostalgia?”
entradas.menu: “You called me here just for nostalgia?”

entradas.text: “Don't tell me Petr Vectern is getting sappy in his old age.”
entradas.menu: “Don't tell me Petr Vectern is getting sappy in his old age.”

entradas.text: “Yes. Erm, no. We'll talk about it. All in good time."
“Not that old! But yes, it happens to the best of us.”
He gestured to the bottle he had in his hand.
I took a swig out of it before passing it back to Petr.
entradas.menu: Drink.

entradas.text: “No, I'm good.”
entradas.menu: “No, I'm good.”

entradas.text: He shrugged, took a very big gulp out of the bottle and staggered to the side afterwards.
He took a very big gulp out of the bottle and staggered to the side afterwards.
“Are you all right?"
entradas.menu: “Are you all right?"

entradas.text: I stayed silent.
entradas.menu: Don't say anything.

entradas.text: “I know you, Petr. What are you hiding?”
entradas.menu: “I know you, Petr. What are you hiding?”

entradas.text: “Yeah. Yeah, I'm okay. Let's go up to the roof. The view was always amazing from there.”
“Let's go up to the roof. The view was always amazing from there.”
“Nothing. Let's go up to the roof. The view was always amazing from there.”
We went up the stairs to the roof. The view was mesmerizing. The buildings of Holsord twinkled below us, while the stars shone bright in the sky.
We sat and leaned back against a wall, taking it all in.
Right as I was starting to get up, I heard a sobbing sound. I turned to Petr and saw tears streaming down his cheeks.
I pretended not to notice his tears.
entradas.menu: Pretend not to notice.

entradas.text: “What's wrong?”
entradas.menu: “What's wrong?”

entradas.text: “I've not yet seen a night sky beautiful enough to make Petr Vectern cry.”
entradas.menu: “I've not yet seen a night sky beautiful enough to make Petr Vectern cry.”

entradas.text: He wiped the tears away and laughed.
He wiped the tears away.
“I messed up Anton. I messed up big time.”
"Evelyn's leaving me. She wants a divorce."
“I'm not surprised."
entradas.menu: “I'm not surprised."

entradas.text: “You two have always had rough patches. I'm sure you'll kiss and make up."
entradas.menu: “You two have always had rough patches. I'm sure you'll kiss and make up."

entradas.text: "What the hell did you do?"
entradas.menu: "What the hell did you do?"

entradas.text: "It's different this time."
“I've been sleeping with Livia Suno.”
“You've been WHAT?!”
entradas.menu: “You've been WHAT?!”

entradas.text: “I know, she's your secretary. I'm so sorry."
“I had a feeling about you two.”
entradas.menu: “I had a feeling about you two.”

entradas.text: “We got careless, I know. I'm so sorry.”
“Shit. What if this causes a scandal?”
entradas.menu: “Shit. What if this causes a scandal?”

entradas.text: “It won't. I'll keep it all under wraps. I'm so sorry."
“How could you do this to me?”
entradas.menu: “How could you do this to me?”

entradas.text: “I will be blunt. You will fix this or I will remove you from office."
entradas.menu: “I will be blunt. You will fix this or I will remove you from office."

entradas.text: “Yes Anton. I understand. Thank you so much."
“All right. It's just an affair, and it's over at that. We can weather this."
entradas.menu: “All right. It's just an affair, and it's over at that. We can weather this."

entradas.text: “You've done enough damage. I will handle it myself.”
entradas.menu: “You've done enough damage. I will handle it myself.”

entradas.text: “Thank you, Anton. That means a lot to me."
Without waiting for his reaction, I left the rooftop alone and made my way downstairs.
On my way out, I grabbed my belongings and took one last look back at the office. It had been home to some happy memories for sure, but this visit had permanently cured me of any nostalgia.
On my way out, I took one last look back at the office. It had been home to some happy memories for sure, but this visit had permanently cured me of any nostalgia.
As soon as I arrived home, I headed up to my study, sat down and stared at the telephone.
I picked up the phone and dialed Lucian's number.
entradas.menu: Call Lucian and tell him what happened.

entradas.text: I headed to the bedroom without calling anyone. Petr and I would be able to handle this between ourselves.
entradas.menu: Trust Petr and call no one.

entradas.text: I stared at the receiver, wondering what his last statement meant. What was going on that I didn't know about?
“Yes, Mr. President.”
I told Lucian everything Petr had told me about himself, Evelyn and Livia.

It was a photograph of me and Monica, sitting under a tree. This must've been 10, maybe 15 years ago. Her expression in it sent pangs through my heart. I couldn't even imagine her looking at me that way now.
“Enough going through old stuff. Let's talk.”
entradas.menu: “Enough going through old stuff. Let's talk.”

entradas.text: “Thanks, but I'd rather not.”
entradas.menu: “Thanks, but I'd rather not.”

entradas.text: “Suit yourself.”
Petr shrugged.
“Yes, yes. All in good time.”
He picked up very quickly.
“Thank you for calling me, Mr. President. This serves to confirm some suspicions of my own. We have to meet.”
The line dropped.
"No, I guess you shouldn't be.”
“It's just, Evelyn hasn't been the same since she lost her job, and Livia was giving me sultry looks from the day I hired her..."
“You were away, I was drunk, one thing led to another."
"But she's more than just a pretty girl, Anton! She's smart and kind... I think we really connected."
"I like her, too. That doesn't mean I'd break my vows and risk a scandal for a bit of horizontal polo!"
entradas.menu: "I like her, too. That doesn't mean I'd break my vows and risk a scandal for a bit of horizontal polo!"

entradas.text: "Don't tell me you're going to run off with her!"
entradas.menu: "Don't tell me you're going to run off with her!"

entradas.text: "No, no. We're ending things. I told her it's too unprofessional. And I want Evelyn back."
"I know, I know. But we're ending things. I told her it's too unprofessional. And I want Evelyn back."
I picked up the phone and dialed Petr's home number.
entradas.menu: Call Evelyn.

entradas.text: "Well, maybe I can speak to Evelyn and plead your case."
entradas.menu: "Well, maybe I can speak to Evelyn and plead your case."

entradas.text: "It's too late. There's still a chance this could get out. I need to talk to Lucian."
entradas.menu: "It's too late. There's still a chance this could get out. I need to talk to Lucian."

entradas.text: "I still can't believe this. I ought to have you both fired."
entradas.menu: "I still can't believe this. I ought to have you both fired."

entradas.text: "Who else knows besides me and the three of you?"
entradas.menu: "Who else knows besides me and the three of you?"

entradas.text: "Nobody, I swear!"
"Anton, please! I'm begging you."
There was an edge of desperation in Petr's voice. He took another drink.
"How many years have we known each other? How many scrapes have we gotten ourselves out of? I can handle this myself. Just trust me and don't bring anyone else into this."
"Anton. You'd do that for me?"
"I'd do it for my best friend. What evidence does she have of the affair?"
entradas.menu: "Of course I would. What evidence does she have of the affair?"

entradas.text: "I'd do it for my presidency. How did Evelyn find out?"
entradas.menu: "No, I'd do it for my administration. How did Evelyn find out?"

entradas.text: "She wrote me a rather saucy note. I made the mistake of putting it in my pants pocket on laundry day."
"Just words. We'll find a way to spin it."
entradas.menu: "Just words. We'll find a way to spin it."

entradas.text: "That's the kind of stupidity that ends presidencies."
entradas.menu: "That's the kind of stupidity that ends presidencies."

entradas.text: "I've known Evelyn almost as long as you. I'll talk some sense into her."
entradas.menu: "I've known Evelyn almost as long as you. I'll talk some sense into her."

entradas.text: Petr's eyes welled up.
"I don't deserve you. Either of you. Thank you for this, Anton."
"Don't worry. Mistakes happen."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry. Mistakes happen."

entradas.text: "Anything for my best friend."
entradas.menu: "Anything for my best friend."

entradas.text: "Don't mention it. I mean it -- *don't mention it*."
entradas.menu: "Don't mention it. I mean it -- *don't mention it*."

entradas.text: "I haven't done anything yet."
entradas.menu: "I haven't done anything yet."

entradas.text: I turned to face my friend and Vice President. The habits that had gotten him dubbed the "bad boy of Sordish politics" when we were young were no longer so charming coming from a middle-aged man. Yet he was still a capable politician, and I couldn't ignore our long history together.
"Don't worry. Mistakes happen."
entradas.menu: "Don't worry. Mistakes happen."

entradas.text: "Anything for my best friend."
entradas.menu: "Anything for my best friend."

entradas.text: "Don't mention it. I mean it -- *don't mention it*."
entradas.menu: "Don't mention it. I mean it -- *don't mention it*."

entradas.text: "Tomorrow?"
entradas.menu: "Tomorrow?"

entradas.text: "Right now?"
entradas.menu: "Right now?"

entradas.text: "What suspicions?"
entradas.menu: "What suspicions?"

entradas.text: "Tomorrow morning in your office. Early, before either of the two arrive."
"I'd rather discuss this in person. Tomorrow morning in your office. Early, before either of the two arrive."
"Yes, but early, before either of the two arrive."
"Don't bring this up with anyone else. I fear we may have more than a mere dalliance on our hands."
I went to bed, but couldn't sleep at all.
I slipped into bed, careful not to disturb my sleeping wife. Petr and Evelyn hadn't made it -- were we next? I hadn't cheated on her, but what I had done was arguably worse...
I couldn't sleep at all that night.
I slipped into bed, careful not to disturb my sleeping wife. Petr and Evelyn hadn't made it -- were we next?
I slipped into bed, careful not to disturb my sleeping wife. I would tell her the news about Petr and Evelyn tomorrow. I hoped it wouldn't upset her too much.
Evelyn answered after a few rings.
"Anton, it's late. Is everything all right?"
I told her what I knew about her, Petr and Livia.
"Oh."
She was silent for so long I thought she might have hung up.
"Whatever you have to say, it won't change my mind."
"Petr still loves you. He was in tears when we talked."
entradas.menu: "Petr still loves you. He was in tears when we talked."

entradas.text: "Don't you understand? Your jealousy could ruin my chances of re-election."
entradas.menu: "Don't you understand? Your jealousy could ruin my chances of re-election."

entradas.text: "He's already ended it. Can't you forgive him?"
entradas.menu: "He's already ended it. Can't you forgive him?"

entradas.text: "Evelyn, please. I didn't call to change your mind. I'm on your side."
entradas.menu: "Evelyn, please. I didn't call to change your mind. I'm on your side."

entradas.text: "You think this is about jealousy?"
Evelyn gave a short, sharp laugh.
"Do you know Petr at all? Really know him?"
"Livia wasn't the first, and she won't be the last. There'll always be another beautiful young woman for him to prey on."
"Preyed on? Livia was a willing participant."
entradas.menu: "Preyed on? Livia was a willing participant."

entradas.text: "That's not fair. Petr says they had a real connection.."
entradas.menu: "That's not fair. Petr says they had a real connection.."

entradas.text: "He has a wandering eye. You knew that when you married him."
entradas.menu: "He has a wandering eye. You knew that when you married him."

entradas.text: "Was she? Look at whom he goes after. Secretaries. Kitchen staff. Aides -- remember Brenda?"
"What do they have in common? When the vice president asks them for sex, they might lose their job if they refuse."
"I thought I could help curb his worst impulses, but it obviously wasn't true. Look at whom he goes after. Secretaries. Kitchen staff. Aides -- remember Brenda?"
"He said that, did he? Look at whom he goes after. Secretaries. Kitchen staff. Aides -- remember Brenda?"
"I'd go to the media about this if I wasn't persona non grata at the Holsord Post. And if there was a shred of a chance I'd be taken seriously."
"But at the very least, I will no longer be an accomplice to his abuse of power. And frankly, Anton, neither should you."
Evelyn hung up without waiting for me to respond. I took a minute to think over what she had said.
Still holding the receiver, I dialled Lucian's number.
entradas.menu: Call Lucian and tell him what happened.

entradas.text: I put down the phone and headed to the bedroom. Nobody else had to get involved in this.
entradas.menu: Put the phone down.

entradas.text: "No need to justify. Men will be men, after all."
entradas.menu: "No need to justify. Men will be men, after all."

entradas.text: "I'm glad you understand. In any case, we're ending things. I told her it's too unprofessional. And I want Evelyn back."
“Ha! That's all? You lucky man!”
entradas.menu: “Ha! That's all? You lucky man!”

entradas.text: “Thanks. I wish my wife saw it that way.”
“No, thank you.”
entradas.menu: “No, thank you.”

entradas.text: “Come on Anton. I insist.”
“I'd rather not.”
entradas.menu: “I'd rather not.”

entradas.text: “Fine...”
"I... I'm sorry. I don't know what to say."
entradas.menu: "I... I'm sorry. I don't know what to say."

entradas.text: Evelyn gave a short, sharp laugh.
"*Now* you're on my side?"
"You're his best friend, Anton. Don't tell me you had no idea what he was getting up to all this time."
"You're right. He behaved despicably, and I did nothing to stop him."
entradas.menu: "You're right. He behaved despicably, and I did nothing to stop him."

entradas.text: "To be fair, neither did I. For years."
"But look at the women he goes after. Secretaries. Kitchen staff. Aides -- remember Brenda?"
"I guess I didn't want to know."
entradas.menu: "I guess I didn't want to know."
